question: What are deep agents?
searches: LangChain deep agents what are deep agents
Deep Agents SDK predefined tools prompts subagents documentation deep agents
answer: In the LangChain ecosystem, Deep Agents refers to an agent “harness” (the Deep Agents SDK) aimed at building more autonomous agents for complex, non-deterministic tasks. In the LangChain docs’ product taxonomy, harnesses sit above agent frameworks/runtimes and provide more “ready-to-run” building blocks like predefined tools, prompts, and subagents. question: When should I use LangGraph instead of LangChain?
searches: When should I use LangGraph instead of LangChain? LangGraph vs LangChain when to use
answer: Use LangGraph instead of (or in addition to) LangChain when you need runtime/orchestration features for production-grade agents, especially: - Low-level control over execution flow (explicit state machines / graphs rather than a mostly linear “agent loop”). - Long-running, stateful workflows/agents (e.g., multi-step processes that may pause and resume). - Durability and persistence (recoverable execution, saving/restoring state). - Streaming and human-in-the-loop (HITL)…

question: How do subagents work in Deep Agents?
searches: Deep Agents subagents how do subagents work
answer: In Deep Agents, “subagents” are separate, fully-specified agents (their own model + tools + optional system prompt) that the main agent can delegate work to via a special task tool that’s injected by middleware. Mechanism: SubAgentMiddleware You enable subagents by adding SubAgentMiddleware(...) to your main agent’s middleware list and providing a list of subagent specs.
